newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks slump on U.S. inflation spook.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks slump on U.S. inflation spook.

text.p: Argentine stocks slumped Thursday on the first trading day of the New Year, as inflation fears reemerged to spook U.S. markets.
"The market was forced to eco the movement of the U.S. long bond on strong U.S. economic indicators," said Jorge Bonanno, an analyst at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip Merval stock index finished 1.55 percent lower at 639.30 points after rebounding slightly towards the close.
The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 10 basis points to 6.74 percent.
"The rise in the yield in the short-term will stop the flow of capital to the region," added Bonanno.
U.S. bonds slumped on the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index, which rose to 54.0 in December from 52.7 a month earlier.
The rise in the index had some analysts fearing the Federal Reserve will raise rates in February.

Of the leading Argentine stocks, 43 fell and five rose on Thursday. The biggest losers of the session were electricity generator Central Puerto that fell 3.5 percent and Telecom Argentina which lost 3.15 percent.
"It was a roller coaster session following the Dow Jones," added Bonanno.

Miguel Daneri, a trader at Boston Securities pointed out that this week's market movements may not be indicative of any new trend because of the closure of the market on Wednesday and Tuesday and thin trading volumes.
